scope: Small-variant creation/decoding section corresponding to VCFv4.5 tables VCF5.10-VCF5.24.

content_comparison.method: Trimmed non-empty source lines compared within the corresponding section ranges; version section line offsets differ. 4.1/4.2 and 4.3/4.4 and 4.4/4.5 normalized line sets are identical in the reviewed ranges; 4.2-to-4.3 contains wording and ordering changes recorded below.
content_comparison.VCFv4_1_to_4_2: No normalized non-empty line differences found in the reviewed section.
content_comparison.VCFv4_3_to_4_4: No normalized non-empty line differences found in the reviewed section.
content_comparison.VCFv4_4_to_4_5: No normalized non-empty line differences found in the reviewed section.

changes.finding: VCFv4.3 adds the explicit sentence 'positions must be sorted in increasing order' immediately before the SNP/deletion/insertion record example.
VCFv4.1/4.2 show the deletion at POS=2 after the SNP at POS=3 in the same example, while VCFv4.3 reorders the records and adds the sorting sentence.
VCFv4.3 rewrites the three example descriptions to specify position 3 and explicit REF/ALT fields; this is a clarity change, not a normalization algorithm.

examples.scope: Small-variant encoding examples: SNP, deletion, insertion and multiallelic representation.
Small-variant decoding examples: SNP, insertion, deletion and mixed microsatellite records.

interpretation_controls: The explicit sorted-position requirement is first observed in the VCFv4.3 small-variant section; do not backfill it into VCFv4.1/4.2 without independent source evidence elsewhere.
The examples show anchoring and REF/ALT construction but do not specify a canonical left-alignment or normalization algorithm.
The source explicitly notes that VCF does not retain the molecular equivalence among bases shown in alignment examples; do not infer preservation of alignment placement.
Example tables are informative; normative force comes from the surrounding prose.
remaining: Independent reviewer must verify whether any other VCFv4.1/4.2 section imposes a record sorting requirement beyond this reviewed small-variant section.
Map the VCFv4.3 sorting clause and REF/ALT anchoring statements to atomic requirement IDs.
Add tests for same-CHROM increasing POS ordering, multiallelic REF/ALT representation and examples that do not imply normalization.
No implementation or test execution is claimed.
